stories.headline: US Federal Reserve raises interest rates to 4% despite demands from Donald Trump
stories.body:
The US Federal Reserve raised its main interest rate on September 16, 2026 [c1]. The central bank voted unanimously to approve the change [c1]. The vote increased the benchmark interest rate by a quarter-percentage point [c1]. This rate now sits in a range between 3.75% and 4% [c1].

US President Donald Trump demanded a rate cut after the decision [c2]. Trump said that interest rates in the United States should be 1% or less [c2].

Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh defended the rate hike [c3]. Warsh said that inflation is too high [c3]. He said that inflation has stayed high for too long [c3].

The Federal Reserve targets an inflation rate of 2% or below [c5]. But US inflation has remained above that target for more than five years [c5]. US consumer price index inflation reached 3.4% in August 2026 [c11]. The Federal Reserve also raised its inflation forecast for 2026 [c10]. The central bank raised the forecast to 3.7% [c10]. Its previous projection was 3.6% [c10].

White House senior deputy press secretary Kush Desai described the rate hike as unfortunate [c9]. Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer also criticized the interest rate increase [c8]. Schumer said the hike will make everything more expensive [c8]. He blamed the economic management of Donald Trump [c8].

Commercial banks moved quickly to adjust their rates after the announcement. Major US banks JP Morgan, KeyCorp, and BNY raised their prime lending rate on Wednesday [c6]. The banks pushed the rate to 7% from 6.75% [c6].

Yields on 10-year US Treasury bonds rose past the 5% threshold after the rate hike announcement [c12].

A majority of Federal Reserve policymakers expect interest rates to be hiked again [c7]. They expect another increase before the end of 2026 [c7]. They project the rate will end up between 4% and 4.25% [c7].

In other action, the US Congress passed new legislation [c4]. Lawmakers passed the Lindsey O Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 in a 262 to 159 vote [c4].

vocab.meaning: with complete agreement from everyone involved

stories.headline: Saudi Arabia accuses Houthis of targeting Mecca as regional tensions escalate
stories.body:
Saudi Arabia accused Yemen's Houthi rebels of launching a drone attack toward Mecca [c14]. Saudi forces intercepted the attempted attack [c14]. Saudi-led coalition spokesperson Turki al-Maliki said the security of the Two Holy Mosques and pilgrims is a red line [c18].

Houthi forces released a video claiming to show a Saudi fighter jet shot down in Marib Governorate [c13]. Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree claimed their forces shot down a Saudi F-15 fighter jet [c17]. Saree said they used a locally made air-to-air missile over Marib province [c17].

Saudi Arabia shut down its East-West pipeline after an attack by Iranian-backed militias in Iraq [c15]. Global crude oil prices remain above $100 a barrel [c16].

US officials held meetings with Houthi leaders over the weekend at the US embassy in Muscat, Oman [c19]. Houthi leaders assured US officials that their 2025 ceasefire holds [c20]. They said they will not target US shipping in the Red Sea [c20]. Suez Canal earnings fell by about $6 billion in 2024 due to Red Sea security disruptions [c21].

vocab.meaning: stopped or caught something before it reached its destination
disturbances that interrupt an event or process

stories.headline: European Union proposes associate membership for Canada in key speech
stories.body:
European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen proposed associate membership for Canada in the European Union [c22]. She made the proposal during her State of the Union address on September 16, 2026 [c22]. Canada would become the first associate member of the European Union under the proposal [c22].

Canada is currently the only non-European country allowed into a major European defense program [c23]. The country can participate in the European Union's 150-billion-euro fund for joint defense purchases [c23]. Canada spends 2% of its gross domestic product on defense [c25]. The nation committed with NATO partners to raise total defense spending to 5% of GDP by 2035 [c25].

Ten of the 27 European Union member states have not yet ratified the free-trade agreement with Canada [c24].

Ursula von der Leyen made other key proposals during her speech. She proposed creating a European Security Council including the United Kingdom and Ukraine [c26]. She also proposed a ban on social media platforms for children under 13 across the European Union [c27].

vocab.meaning: joined with others in a partial or official partnership
formally approved or agreed to a contract or treaty

stories.headline: Hague tribunal sentences former Kosovo President Hashim Thaçi to 25 years for war crimes
stories.body:
The Specialist Court in The Hague found former Kosovo President Hashim Thaçi guilty of war crimes [c28]. The Kosovo Specialist Chambers sentenced Thaçi and former Kosovo Liberation Army leader Jakup Krasniqi to 25 years in prison each [c29]. The court sentenced former KLA leaders Kadri Veseli to 18 years and Rexhep Selimi to 13 years [c30].

Judges convicted Thaçi and his co-defendants of arbitrary detention of 385 people [c33]. The court found them guilty of cruel treatment of 49 people and torture of 303 detainees [c33]. They were also convicted of the murder of 96 people [c33].

Kosovo Prime Minister Albin Kurti called the convictions and sentences an unacceptable injustice [c31]. Dutch riot police detained two people after clashes with Thaçi supporters outside the court [c34]. The 1998-1999 Kosovo War left about 13,000 people dead, including about 9,000 ethnic Albanian Kosovars [c35].

In Sweden's election, the left-leaning opposition is projected to win 176 seats in parliament compared to 173 for the governing coalition and Sweden Democrats [c32].

stories.headline: US lawmaker places hold on $2.8 billion arms package to Israel
stories.body:
US Representative Gregory Meeks placed a hold on a proposed $2.8 billion arms transfer to Israel [c36]. The proposed weapons package includes 20,000 MK-84 bombs [c37]. It also includes 20,000 BLU-117 bombs and 20,000 I-2000 penetrator warheads [c37].

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio declared a national security emergency in 2025 [c38]. That declaration bypassed congressional review to fast-track nearly $3 billion in weapons sales to Israel [c38].

The Biden administration paused a shipment of 2,000-pound bombs to Israel in 2024 [c39]. Donald Trump reversed that decision after taking office in January 2025 [c39].

Opposition to military support for Israel has grown among some lawmakers in Washington. More than 100 House Democrats voted in July 2026 to end US military assistance to Israel [c40].

a serious situation requiring immediate action

stories.headline: Damaged buildings collapse in Gaza, killing dozens of residents
stories.body:
A war-damaged building collapsed in Gaza City's Tal al-Hawa area, killing at least 21 people [c42]. The six-story building had been damaged by a prior Israeli strike [c42]. Eight children were among those killed in the collapse [c42].

Another war-damaged seven-story building collapsed in Gaza, killing at least 20 people [c41]. Nine members of Hayat al-Ajlah's extended family died when the al-Saada building collapsed in western Gaza City [c47].

United Nations Development Programme Gaza head Alessandro Mrakic issued a warning about structural dangers [c43]. Mrakic warned that around 400 war-damaged buildings across Gaza face imminent risk of collapse [c43].

Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz said 70% of Gaza's population was emptied from homes during the military offensive [c46]. More than 73,790 people have been killed in Gaza since October 7, 2023, according to Gaza's health ministry [c44]. The ministry reported that 1,369 Palestinians were killed and 4,627 wounded since the ceasefire took effect on October 11, 2025 [c45].

vocab.meaning: an aggressive military attack or operation

stories.headline: Pakistani corvette collides with Indian warship in Arabian Sea, triggering protests
stories.body:
A Pakistani naval corvette collided with an Indian warship in the North Arabian Sea on September 15, 2026 [c48]. The incident occurred in the evening involving Pakistan Navy vessel PNS Hunain [c48]. The Pakistani ship hit a frontline Indian Navy warship [c48].

The collision caused different levels of damage to the two vessels. PNS Hunain sustained damage during the impact [c50]. The Pakistani corvette returned to harbour after the collision [c50]. The Indian vessel suffered minor damage [c50]. It continued its routine surveillance mission [c50].

A source told the Times of India about the actions of the Indian commander [c58]. The source said the captain of the Indian warship exercised extreme restraint to prevent a severe accident [c58].

Both countries lodged formal diplomatic protests following the collision. The Indian Ministry of External Affairs summoned Pakistan's Chargé d'Affaires in New Delhi [c49]. India delivered a strong diplomatic protest over the incident [c49].

India claimed the Pakistani ship broke a long-standing military agreement [c51]. The Ministry of External Affairs said the Pakistani vessel violated Article 10 of a 1991 pact [c51]. That agreement is the Agreement on Advance Notice on Military Exercises, Manoeuvres and Troops Movements [c51]. Article 10 mandates that naval ships and submarines maintain a distance of at least three nautical miles [c54]. The rule aims to prevent accidents in international waters [c54].

Pakistan also lodged a diplomatic protest over the collision. Pakistan's foreign ministry summoned Indian Chargé d'Affaires Satyanjal Pandey late on Wednesday night [c55]. Pakistan summoned the diplomat in Islamabad [c52]. Pakistani officials called the collision a highly provocative action [c52]. They said the incident occurred inside Pakistan's exclusive economic zone [c52].

PNS Hunain is a Yarmook-class offshore patrol vessel [c53]. Damen Shipyards built the vessel in Romania [c53]. The Pakistan Navy commissioned the ship in July 2024 [c53].

This collision marks the first reported military incident between the two nations since May 2025 [c56]. That earlier period involved four days of hostilities following the Pahalgam terror attack [c56]. The last recorded collision between warships of the two nations occurred in June 2011 [c57]. During that incident, PNS Babur touched INS Godavari during an anti-piracy patrol in the Gulf of Aden [c57].

vocab.meaning: a small, fast warship used for patrol or escort
close observation of an area or activity
controlled or unemotional behavior in a situation

stories.headline: Indian government rules out rollback of 0.4% UPI merchant transaction charges
stories.body:
The Union government ruled out any rollback of new charges on digital payments [c64]. A 0.4 per cent Merchant Discount Rate will apply to UPI merchant payments of ₹2,000 or more [c67]. The government set the start date for October 15, 2026 [c64]. The fee is capped at ₹300 for transactions of ₹75,000 or more [c67]. Small merchants receiving up to ₹1 lakh per month through UPI QR payments are excluded [c68]. Merchant transactions up to Rs 2,000 and all person-to-person transfers remain free [c65]. Capital market payments will face a 0.02% rate capped at ₹300, while specified essential sectors face a flat ₹5 charge [c69].

Opposition leader Rahul Gandhi criticized Prime Minister Narendra Modi over the policy [c61]. Gandhi called the framework a UPI tax [c61]. Five Congress MPs served on the parliamentary committee that recommended the framework [c63]. The Parliamentary Standing Committee on Finance presented its report on August 12, 2026 [c62]. The committee adopted the report without recorded dissent [c63].

Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister Omar Abdullah backed the decision [c59]. Abdullah said operating digital payment infrastructure is costly [c59]. Abdullah noted person-to-person money transfers carry no charge [c60].

Legal and retail challenges have emerged. Advocate Anjan Datta filed a public interest litigation in the Supreme Court to stop the framework [c66]. Retailers Association of India CEO Kumar Rajagopalan said small merchants will think twice about accepting cash or UPI [c71]. The Clothing Manufacturers Association of India expressed concern over extra pressure during the festive season [c72].
